5 years ago today, Dune premiered.

Denis Villeneuve first discovered the world of Dune around age twelve after reading Frank Herbert's 1965 novel and learning about David Lynch's 1984 film adaptation through the sci-fi magazines Fantastic Films and Starlog. He wanted to make a faithful adaptation, so he waited until he'd done the science-fiction films Arrival (2016) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) first so that he would have sufficient experience in the genre before starting work on this film. In fact, scenes from his prior films are strongly influenced by his interpretations of scenes from the novel.

Dune: Part Three is scheduled to release in theaters on December 18, 2026. Set roughly 12 to 17 years into Paul Atreides' ruthless reign as Emperor, following the fallout of the galaxy-wide holy war, growing conspiracies, and his deepening isolation. Are you excited about it? 💭
